gloss: have no recourse; nothing can be done; at a loss

definitions.gloss: have no recourse; nothing can be done; no way to deal with it
definitions.explanation: An expression meaning there are no available measures or strategies to resolve a problem. Literally 'there is no move to play,' from the game of go or shogi.

examples.japanese: ⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧{打|う}つ{手|て}がない。
examples.english: There's nothing more we can do.
The doctor said nothing more could be done.

examples.japanese: ⟦{赤字|あかじ}→赤字：04712_akaji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}き→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧、⟦{経営陣|けいえいじん}→経営陣：20535_keieijin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{打|う}つ{手|て}がない⟦{状態|じょうたい}→状態：03345_joutai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{追|お}い{込|こ}まれた→追い込む：06371_oikomu⟧。
examples.english: Losses continued, and the management was driven into a state where nothing could be done.

notes:
Literally "there is no move to play" — a metaphor from board games (go, shogi) where no viable move remains. Expresses helplessness in the face of a problem that cannot be solved.

FORMS:
- ⟦{打|う}つ{手|て}→打つ手：30191_utsute⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧なくなる: to run out of options
- ⟦{打|う}つ{手|て}→打つ手：30191_utsute⟧なし: no recourse (more concise form)
- ⟦{打|う}つ{手|て}→打つ手：30191_utsute⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{失|うしな}う→失う：01887_ushinau⟧: to lose all options

- ⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{施|ほどこ}し→施す：12985_hodokosu⟧よう⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧: nothing can be done (more formal)

ETYMOLOGY:
From board game terminology — ⟦{打|う}つ{手|て}→打つ手：30191_utsute⟧ refers to a move or play one can make. When there are no more moves available, one has lost.
